name: Ming dynasty
region: China; regional variation, with Jingdezhen specifically for porcelain contexts
summary: Long dynasty with strong court, scholar-painting, furniture, textile and ceramic evidence; the late Ming visual world differs materially from the early Ming.

wardrobe.text: role-specific Ming robes and civilian garments; do not default to theatrical wuxia robes

hairstyle_headwear.text: select adult hairstyle/headwear by sex/status and subperiod; avoid Qing queue

architecture.text: courtyard/garden/town contexts with timber construction and masonry surfaces

interior_furniture.text: hardwood tables, chairs, cabinets and screens in affluent settings

weapons_tools.text: jian/dao and practical martial equipment in appropriate roles

transportation.text: horse, sedan chair, boat depending on region/status

writing_calligraphy.text: scholar calligraphy/painting contexts; exact visible text should be verified

lighting_technology.text: lamps/candles/lanterns for interiors and night scenes

visual_arts.text: scholar painting in ink on paper
court painting in ink/color on silk

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: fantasy flying sword as historical martial practice
Tang court styling as generic Ming

prompt_fragments.wuxia: Ground the wuxia fiction in Ming material life first: plausible travel clothing, practical footwear, a single traceable weapon, timber/masonry setting, and human-scale action; then add genre tension without supernatural effects.

sources.supports: Ming art/material examples including painting, embroidery, porcelain and furniture
cobalt underglaze and Jingdezhen blue-and-white process/history

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict mode should narrow early/middle/late Ming, region, role/status, and exact object/garment evidence.
